summary: Naftopidil is a selective alpha-1 adrenoceptor antagonist used to relieve lower urinary tract symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). It has relatively high affinity for the alpha-1D adrenoceptor subtype (and also blocks alpha-1A), relaxing smooth muscle in the prostate, prostatic capsule, bladder neck and urethra, which reduces bladder outlet resistance and improves urinary flow and storage symptoms. It is taken orally once daily after food, usually starting at 25 mg and titrating to 50-75 mg according to response and tolerability. Naftopidil is marketed mainly in Japan and parts of Asia and is not FDA-approved, so dosing follows local manufacturer labelling and clinical practice. The principal adverse effects are dizziness, orthostatic hypotension and (as with other uroselective alpha-blockers) the intraoperative floppy iris syndrome during cataract surgery, so ophthalmologists should be told of its use.

moa: Naftopidil is a selective antagonist of alpha-1 adrenoceptors with relatively greater affinity for the alpha-1D subtype compared with alpha-1A and alpha-1B. Alpha-1 adrenoceptors mediate sympathetic tone in the smooth muscle of the prostate, prostatic urethra and bladder neck; the alpha-1D subtype is also abundant in the bladder body. By blocking these receptors, naftopidil relaxes prostatic and bladder-outlet smooth muscle, lowering urethral resistance and improving urinary flow, and may also improve storage (irritative) symptoms. It has little effect on prostate size and does not lower serum prostate-specific antigen.

pearls: Uroselective alpha-1 blocker with relative alpha-1D selectivity - eases both voiding and storage BPH symptoms
Marketed mainly in Japan/Asia; not FDA-approved, so dosing follows local labelling (start 25 mg, titrate to 50-75 mg once daily)
Take after food in the evening and warn patients of first-dose/orthostatic hypotension
Class effect: intraoperative floppy iris syndrome - inform the ophthalmologist before cataract surgery
Does not reduce prostate size or serum PSA; additive hypotension with PDE-5 inhibitors and antihypertensives
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it and continue as normal. Do not take two doses together.
overdose: Overdose is expected to cause exaggerated hypotension, dizziness and reflex tachycardia. There is no specific antidote. Management is supportive: lie the patient down with legs elevated, give intravenous fluids, and use vasopressors if needed; monitor blood pressure and heart rate. Dialysis is unlikely to be helpful given high protein binding.
